policies.policy_name: Role‑Based Deletion Permission for Incident SLA
policies.description: Only users with the Administrator role are authorized to delete Incident SLA records because only the Administrator has full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. Manager and Agent roles have CRUD only on limited tables that do not include SLA tables, so they lack delete permission for Incident SLA records.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.

Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations.

Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. | Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings.

policies.description: If a user attempts to delete Incident SLA records without having the required Administrator role, the operation must be halted and a 403 Forbidden error returned, indicating that the user role lacks authority for the operation.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.policy_name: No Fabrication of IDs for Deletion
policies.description: When deleting Incident SLA records, the assistant must never assume, fabricate, or guess SLA record IDs. It must rely only on verified IDs obtained from prior API calls or trusted sources before issuing a delete request.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.

policies.description: Each delete_incident_slas call must be performed as a single validated operation. The assistant may not combine deletion with other actions unless using an approved batch endpoint, ensuring the operation is atomic.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.description: If a deletion attempt fails because the Incident SLA record is locked or in a state that prevents removal, the assistant must return a 409 Conflict error to indicate the state conflict.
references: 409 Conflict: Record locking or state conflict.

policies.description: If the delete_incident_slas operation exceeds API rate limits, the assistant must pause and retry using exponential backoff rather than immediately retrying or continuing.
references: Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

policies.description: If a request to delete Incident SLA records violates any governing rule (e.g., missing required filters, insufficient role), the assistant must halt the operation and return the specific policy reason before pausing.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.description: The assistant may proceed with the deletion of Incident SLA records without asking the user for additional confirmation, provided all policy checks (role, filters, ID verification) are satisfied.
references: You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.
